Through: Mr. Syed Manzoor Ahmad, Advocate with
Mr. Saqib Khan, Advocate.
Vs.
Kumar Rajiv Ranjan and Ors
...Respondent(s).
Through: Mr. G.N. Sofi, AAG.
CORAM:
HON’BLE MR. JUSTICE MOHD YOUSUF WANI, JUDGE
ORDER
22.09.2026
1. This contempt petition came to be filed before this Court way back
in December, 2014 for proceeding against the respondents/alleged
contemnors for their alleged willful defiance and the breach of the
judgment of this Court dated 25.07.2024 passed in OWP No.
1369/2014. The judgment, for the alleged defiance and breach of
which, the instant contempt petition stands filed so as to proceed
against the alleged contemnors in accordance with the law, directs
the respondents in the basic petition to process and settle the case of
the petitioners for payment of compensation qua the land in
question measuring 1 Kanal and 9 and a Half Marla covered under
Survey No. 323 Min situated at Shalimar Bagh strictly in tune with
the directions passed by this Court on 12.02.2014 in OWP No.
864/2012. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners
that vide order dated 12.02.2014 passed on OWP No. 864/2012,

while disposing of the same, the respondents were directed to verify
the title of the petitioners vis-à-vis the subject land and, subject to
the verification, pay the reasonable compensation to be decided by
the Collector at the prevalent market rate. It is submitted that while
misinterpreting the said judgment to the prejudice and injustice of
the petitioners, the respondents proceeded to pass the order No.
Divcom/RA-AVS (10) 2014 dated: 16.05.2014 denying their lawful
claim, which prompted the petitioners to approach again before this
Court with the subsequent petition OWP 1369/2014. That finally
while disposing of the aforesaid petition, the order dated 16.05.2014
was quashed with the direction to the respondents to process and
settle the case of the petitioners for payment of compensation vis-à-
vis the subject land directly in time with the directions passed earlier
by this Court in OWP No. 864/2012 in terms of the judgment dated
12.02.2014. The respondents were directed to complete the exercise
preferably within a period of three months from the date a copy of
the judgment dated 25.07.2024 is produced before them.
2. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the judgment dated
25.07.2024 passed with clarification and unequivocal direction to the
respondents is still awaiting its compliance at the hands of the
respondents.
3. Tehsildar (North) Srinagar who was the respondent No. 4 in the
main petition, is present along with the record and has submitted in
the open court, on the basis of the perusal of the record, that
petitioners are the owners of the subject land which is recorded as

bedzar and has already been taken over by the Government in
connection with the development of the park. It is submitted by the
learned counsel for the petitioners that the park developed on the
land of the petitioners was earlier looked after by the Floriculture
Department but now falls within the domain of Srinagar Municipal
Corporation
4. The impleadment of the present incumbent in the Office of the
Commissioner Srinagar Municipal Corporation Faz Lul Haseeb
(IAS) appears to be imperative for the just disposal of the instant
contempt petition.
5. The former Divisional Commissioner, Kashmir, stands already
arrayed as contemnor in the instant petition.
6. The present Divisional Commissioner, Kashmir Mr. Anshul Garg
(IAS) is also impleaded as party respondent in the contempt petition.
7. As per the judgment in question, the respondents therein were
directed to pay the compensation to the petitioners to be assessed by
the Collector concerned at the market rate.
8. Now in the facts and circumstances of the case, the newly impleaded
persons namely Anchul Garg, Divisional Commissioner, Kashmir
and Faz Lul Haseeb, Commissioner, Srinagar Municipal
Coroportion have to account for the implementation of the judgment
in question
9. Both these persons stand impleaded as respondents in the contempt
petition.

10. Registry is directed to issue notices to both the respondents in the
contempt petition supported with the copies of the petition and the
judgment dated 25.07.2024, for filing the compliance
report/statement of facts by the next date of hearing.
11. List on 28th October, 2026.
12. Tehsildar (North) Srinagar is relieved and his personal appearance
for the time being is dispensed with.
(MOHD YOUSUF WANI)
JUDGE
SRINAGAR
22.09.2026
Shahid Manzoor

AT SRINAGAR
WP(C) No. 2085/2026
CM No. (5637/2026)
Afshin Khan …Petitioner/Appellant(s)
Through: Mr. Mir Mohsin Ali, Advocate
Vs.
Union of India And Ors. ...Respondent(s)
Through: Ms. Yasmeen Jan, Advocate vice
Mr. T. M. Shamsi, DSGI
CORAM: HON’BLE MR. JUSTICE SANJAY PARIHAR, JUDGE
ORDER
07.09.2026
1. The petitioner is an accused in FIR No. 337/2025, registered for the
commission of offences under Section 8/23-B of the Immigration
and Foreigners Act, 2025 (hereinafter referred to as “the Act” or “the
Special Act”). The prosecution case, in essence, is that the petitioner
failed to report, in the prescribed Form-C (Form-III), the stay of a
foreign national at his homestay, as required under the Rules framed
under the Act. The alleged omission is stated to have attracted the
aforesaid penal provisions, culminating in the presentation of the
charge-sheet dated 29.12.2025, which is presently pending
consideration before the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Budgam.
WP(C) No. 2085/2026 Page 1 of 7

2. The case set up by the petitioner is that, by virtue of Section 25 of the
Act, the offences alleged against him are compoundable and that the
competent authority, namely respondent No. 2-Foreigners Regional
Registration Officer (FRRO), Amritsaris empowered to compound
the specified offence either before or after the institution of
prosecution. It is pleaded that the petitioner had approached
respondent No. 4- Foreigners Registration Officer, Budgam by way
of an appropriate representation/application seeking compounding of
the offence. However, no decision thereon was taken, compelling the
petitioner to invoke the writ jurisdiction of this Court.
3. During the course of hearing, ld. counsel for the petitioner submitted
that the grievance of the petitioner lies in a narrow compass. It was
submitted that since the petitioner has already approached the
competent authority seeking compounding of the offence, the
petitioner would be satisfied if the present petition is disposed of
with a direction to the concerned authority to consider and decide his
request for compounding in accordance with law.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents opposed the petition
and submitted that, although the offences in question are
compoundable, the remedy available to the petitioner is to approach
the Trial Court for compounding of the offence in accordance with
law. It was further contended that even if, as a matter of procedure,
an application for compounding is required to be moved by the
complainant or the competent authority, the petitioner is not
remediless. According to the respondents, the petitioner may avail
himself of the remedy of plea bargaining as contemplated under
WP(C) No. 2085/2026 Page 2 of 7

Chapter XXI-A (Sections 265-A to 265-L) of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973. It was, accordingly, argued that an equally
efficacious alternative remedy is available to the petitioner and,
therefore, invocation of the extraordinary writ jurisdiction of this
Court is unwarranted.
5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considered the
material on record, it emerges that, as on date, the petitioner is facing
prosecution pursuant to the charge-sheet presented for the
commission of offences under Sections 8/23-B of the Act, which is
presently pending before the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Budgam. It is not in dispute that the offence in question is
compoundable under the Act. The petitioner also appears to have
approached the Senior Superintendent of Police, Budgam the
Investigating Agency seeking compounding of the offence. In
response thereto, vide communication dated 29.04.2026, the
petitioner was advised to approach the Trial Court for appropriate
directions with regard to compounding of the offence in accordance
with the procedure prescribed under Section 25 of the Act, including
the requirement of obtaining approval of the Government of India,
wherever so required.
6. The petitioner, in essence, seeks issuance of a writ of mandamus
commanding respondents Nos. 1 to 4 to process his case for
compounding of the offence. The question that, therefore, arises for
consideration is whether such a mandamus can be issued at the
instance of the petitioner. The answer has necessarily to be in the
negative, for the respondents cannot be said to be under a
WP(C) No. 2085/2026 Page 3 of 7

corresponding statutory obligation to compound the offence merely
at the asking of the petitioner. The counsel for the petitioner,
however, invited the attention of this Court to an order passed by the
Hon’ble High Court of Kerala in WP(Crl.) No. 1405/2025, whereby
the writ petition therein came to be disposed of with a direction
permitting/requiring the petitioner to submit an application
containing the necessary particulars for compounding of the offence.
7. This Court has heard learned counsel for the petitioner on the
aforesaid aspect and has also carefully gone through the judgment
cited at the Bar. Since the offence for which the petitioner is being
prosecuted is an offence under a special enactment, the procedure
governing its investigation, inquiry and trial has to be understood in
the light of Section 4(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023 (“BNSS”). Section 4(2) of the BNSS, in substance, provides
that offences under any law other than the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita,
2023 (“BNS”) are to be investigated, inquired into, tried and
otherwise dealt with in accordance with the provisions of the BNSS,
subject, however, to any enactment for the time being in force
regulating the manner or place of investigating, inquiring into, trying
or otherwise dealing with such offences. Consequently, where the
Special Act prescribes a particular procedure, such procedure would
govern; and in matters on which the Special Act is silent, the
provisions of the BNSS would apply.
8. Section 25 of the Special Act makes a specific provision for
compounding of certain offences, including offences punishable
under Sections 21, 23 and 24 of the Act. The provision enables the
WP(C) No. 2085/2026 Page 4 of 7

specified offences to be compounded, either before the institution of
prosecution or during the course of trial, by such officer or authority
as may be duly authorised in that behalf. Sub-section (3) further
provides that every officer or authority referred to in sub-section (1)
shall exercise the power of compounding subject to the direction,
control and supervision of the Central Government.
9. The statutory scheme further contemplates that where an offence is
compounded after institution of prosecution or during the course of
trial, the factum of such compounding is required to be brought by
the competent authority to the notice of the Court before which the
prosecution or trial is pending. Upon such intimation being given, the
individual, company or organisation, or the officer or employee
thereof, as the case may be, in relation to whom the offence has been
compounded, is to be discharged in accordance with law. Thus,
Section 25 envisages a statutory mechanism for compounding of
specified offences by the authority duly empowered in that behalf,
subject to the conditions and supervisory framework contemplated
by the Act.
10. In the present case, no application seeking compounding of the
offence appears to have been moved by the petitioner before the
learned Trial Court, notwithstanding the fact that the prosecution is
already pending before it. Instead, the petitioner has invoked the
extraordinary writ jurisdiction of this Court seeking a direction to the
respondents to process his request for compounding. The mere fact
that an offence is compoundable does not, by itself, confer upon an
accused an indefeasible right to have the offence compounded.
WP(C) No. 2085/2026 Page 5 of 7

Compounding has to take place in the manner contemplated by the
statute and through the authority empowered by law to exercise such
power.
11. At the same time, there can be no quarrel with the proposition that
where the State or an authority constituted by it is vested with the
statutory power to consider compounding of an offence, such power
is required to be exercised fairly, reasonably and in accordance with
the procedure prescribed by law. This, however, would not entitle the
petitioner, in the facts of the present case, to seek a writ commanding
the respondents to compound the offence or to process the matter in a
particular manner dehors the statutory procedure.
12. Once the charge-sheet has been presented and the criminal
proceedings are pending before the competent Trial Court, it would
be appropriate for the petitioner to approach the said Court with an
application seeking such relief as may be permissible under law.
Upon such an application being moved, it shall be open to the Trial
Court, having regard to the statutory scheme under Section 25 of the
Act, to deal with the same in accordance with law and, where
necessary, call upon the competent compounding authority to take
such steps as are contemplated under the Act. In these circumstances,
no case for exercise of the extraordinary writ jurisdiction of this
Court is made out.
13. For the foregoing reasons, this Court finds no merit in the present
petition. The same is, accordingly, dismissed.
14. It is, however, made clear that dismissal of the present petition shall
not preclude the petitioner from moving an appropriate application
WP(C) No. 2085/2026 Page 6 of 7

before the Trial Court seeking compounding of the offence. In the
event such an application is filed, the Trial Court shall consider and
deal with the same, in accordance with law, having regard to the
provisions of Section 25 of the Act and without being influenced by
the dismissal of the present writ petition.
(SANJAY PARIHAR)

1. There is a delay of Four (04) days in filing the Review Petition
seeking to review the order and judgment dated 20th November,
2024, passed by this Court in LPAOW No. 92/2018 titled, “Abdul
Hamid Dandroo and Ors vs State of J and K and Ors”.
2. Application, for the reasons stated therein, is allowed, and the delay
of four days in filing the Review Petition is condoned.
3. This application is disposed of.
RP 95/2024
1. This is a petition seeking review of the judgment dated 20th
November, 2024 passed in LPAOW No. 92/2018, titled, “Abdul
Hamid Dandroo and Ors vs State of J and K and Ors”, on the
ground that this Court has not considered the matter in its right
perspective.
2. The review is sought, inter alia, on the ground that, consequent
upon dismissal of the appeal, the petitioners have been left with no

efficacious remedy to avail of. It is further contended that, despite
writ petitions involving similar questions of law and fact being
pending adjudication before this Court, the appeal filed by the
petitioners came to be dismissed by virtue of the judgment dated
20th November, 2024, which is the subject matter of the present
review petition.
3. After arguing for a while, the learned counsel appearing for the
petitioners fairly submitted that similar writ petitions have now
been dismissed and, therefore, the ground urged in this regard is not
available.
4. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and perused the
material on record, this Court is of the opinion that no good ground
is made out to recall the judgment dated 20th November, 2024
(supra).
5. This Court has already held that the petitioners have been pursuing
the matter before the Civil Court and having regard to the fact that
issues raised by the petitioners involve determination of
complicated disputed questions of fact, a civil suit is the appropriate
remedy. This Court has thus rightly declined to invoke the
extraordinary jurisdiction vested in it under Article 226 of the
Constitution of India and has, accordingly, dismissed the appeal as
being devoid of any merit.
6. The review petition does not disclose any error apparent on the
record, committed by this Court, while dismissing the appeal vide
judgment dated 20th November, 2024, nor there is any discovery of

new facts which would persuade us to take a view different from
the one already taken for the disposal of the appeal.
7. For all these reasons, we find no merit in this petition and the same
is, accordingly, dismissed.

(ORDER)
26.09.2026
1. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner in respect of the
matter.
2. The case of the petitioner, in nutshell, is that he and his brother
are reputed businessmen who are running multiple ventures across
the globe, including the FIL Industries, having its substantial
business in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. That he,
through his firm, i.e., FIL Industries Private Limited, has availed
various loan facilities from Large Credit Unit of Jammu & Kashmir
Bank Private Limited for smooth operation of his ventures, in
connection whereof multiple mortgage deeds have been executed by
him in favour of the Jammu & Kashmir Bank Private Limited as
collateral security. That in the year 2022, he applied for enhancement
of cash credit limit from Rs. 70.22 crores to rupees 76.22 Crores to
upgrade and modernize its existing food and beverage division at
SIDCO electronics complex at Rangreth, and also to enhance its

Page No. 02
WP(C) No. 2423/2026
working capital facility. That a mortgage deed as collateral security
dated 28-07-2022 was executed and registered with Sub-Registrar
Sopore in favour of the Jammu & Kashmir Bank Private Limited on
06-10-2022. That stamp duty and registration fees for the aforesaid
mortgage deed dated 28-07-2022 was exempted in pursuance of the
Government Notification No. SO241 dated 16th of July, 2021,
whereby the Government directed that there shall be remission of
duty chargeable under the Stamps Act, 1977, for new as well as
existing industrial units undertaking substantial expansion in case of
documents/ instruments related to land transactions in Government
Industrial Estates, including lease/ mortgage deeds executed by the
said industrial units under Jammu & Kashmir Industrial Policy 2021-
30, notified by the Government vide Order No. 117-IND of 2021,
dated 19th April, 2021.
That he and his brother again, in the year 2022, applied for
grant of ad hoc loan facility, whereupon the Jammu & Kashmir Bank
Private Limited, sanctioned the said facility to the tune of rupees 10
Crore over and above the already sanctioned limit, in connection
whereof the mortgage deed dated 28-10-2022 was executed and
registered before the Sub-Registrar Sopore on 14-11-2022. That the
stamp duty and registration fees on the said mortgage deed was again
exempted by the said office of the Sub-Registrar concerned in
pursuance to the aforesaid Government Notification dated 16th of
July, 2021, forming Annexure- I to the petition.
That on 12-05-2023, Government issued a clarification with
respect to the Government Order No. 117-IND of 2021, dated 19th of

Page No. 03
WP(C) No. 2423/2026
April, 2021, pertaining to exemption of stamp duty and registration
fees, of industrial units, within the jurisdiction of industrial estate
whose mortgaged property falls outside the Government Industrial
Estate, and directed that where the industrial units falling within the
industrial estate but the proposed mortgage property falls outside the
industrial estate would not be exempted from the payment of stamp
duty and registration fees. That the copy of the said clarification
order issued by the Government has been annexed to the petition as
Annexure- III.
That again, in the year 2023, the Jammu & Kashmir Bank
sanctioned a short-term loan of rupees 8 Crores in his favour against
the mortgage deed that came to be executed on 19-07-2023 and
registered before the learned Sub-Registrar Sopore on 31-07-
2023.That he, as per the clarification order/ communication dated 12-
05-2023 dated 19th of April, 2021 issued by the Government
regarding payment of stamp duty and registration fees, accordingly
paid rupees 4 lacs as stamp duty and 9.60 lacs as registration fees.
That the copy of the said mortgage deed dated 19-07-2023 is annexed
with his petition and marked as Annexure IV.
That he, time and again, approached the respondents seeking
clarification as regards the liability of stamp duty and registration
fees in respect of the mortgage deeds executed by him and his brother
in the year 2022, when the stamp duty and registration fee were
exempted by the office of the learned Sub-Registrar in pursuance of
the then existing Government Notification dated 16th July, 2021. That
he, however, paid the stamp duty as required by the office of the Sub-

Page No. 04
WP(C) No. 2423/2026
Registrar concerned on the mortgage deed executed and registered
subsequently to the clarification order/ communication dated 12-05-
2023. That he has voluntary under a bona fide intention, approached
the Office of the concerned Sub-Registrar to seek clarification as to
whether he needs to pay the registration fee and stamp duty on the
earlier mortgage deeds or not. That ambiguity regarding the order of
exemption and the subsequent revocation of the same still persists, as
the earlier order of exemption had been issued by the learned
Financial Commissioner to the Government, Department of Finance,
when the subsequent order of clarification of the said order of
exemption was issued by the Inspector General of Registration. That
he has already filed a representation with the respondents seeking
clarification as to whether the order revoking the exemption would
apply retrospectively to the deeds executed in the year 2022, for
which no stamp duty and registration fee was chargeable, and
expressed his intention that he is ready to pay the stamp duty and
registration fee also on such earlier mortgage deeds, if at all required
under law.
3. The petitioner has accordingly prayed for the issuance of
writs/ orders in the nature of mandamus:-
1) for commanding the respondents to decide his application/
representation seeking clarification as to whether the order
dated 12-05-2023, issued by respondent No. 3, revoking the
exemption of stamp duty and registration fee in respect of
the mortgaged property situated outside the Industrial Units,
would operate retrospectively and would cover the

Page No. 05
WP(C) No. 2423/2026
mortgage deeds executed by him and his brother in the year
2022 and registered before the learned Sub-Registrar,
Sopore.
2) for directing the respondents to require and receive from
him the proper stamp and registration fee on such earlier
mortgage deeds, if required in accordance with law.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioner, during his preliminary
arguments, submitted that the petitioner and his brother are
awakened, well-reputed, highly respected and law-abiding citizens,
who have volunteered to approach the respondents seeking the
clarification as regards the payment of stamp duty and registration
fee in respect of the mortgage deeds executed by them in favour of
Jammu & Kashmir Bank Private Limited in consideration of loan
facilities, prior to the passing of the clarification order dated 12-05-
2023, and have shown their willingness to pay the requisite stamp
duty and registration fee, if so required to be paid in respect of the
earlier mortgage deeds, on which the said duties were exempted by
the office of the concerned Sub-Registrar in pursuance of
Government Order No. 117-IND of 2021 dated 19th of April, 2021.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the instant
petition, in view of its facts and the relief sought herein, can be
disposed of even at this threshold stage by passing of appropriate
directions, which are likely to be in the interest of the respondents,
and the action under which directions was already needed to be taken
under rules by the respondents out of their statutory obligations,
especially upon being represented by the petitioner.

Page No. 06

6. In the facts and circumstances of the case, the Court is of the
opinion that, as rightly suggested by the learned counsel for the
petitioner, the matter can be disposed of even at this threshold stage
by passing of appropriate directions, which will be advantageous to
the respondents/ UT of J&K.
7. For the foregoing discussion, the instant petition is disposed

and 4, i.e., Inspector General of Registration, Jammu and Kashmir
and Sub-Registrar, Sopore, District Baramulla, to address the
application/representation of the petitioner, already filed or to be filed
by him, seeking clarification regarding his liability to pay the stamp
duty and registration fee on the mortgage deeds executed by him and
his brother and registered by the learned Sub-Registrar, Sopore,
Baramulla, prior to the clarification Order/Communication dated 12-
05- 2023, revoking the exemption already availed by them on such
earlier mortgage deeds in pursuance of Government Order No. 117-
IND of 2021 (SO241) dated 19th of April, 2021, and to require and
receive the proper stamp duty/ registration fee from them, if at all
required under law. The respondents Nos. 3 and 4 are directed to take
action in the matter within a period of eight weeks
8. Disposed of.

CM No. 03/2026:
By virtue of the instant application, the writ petitioner seeks revival of the
main writ petition, which came to be dismissed vide order dated 07.05.2016 on
the basis of the statement made by learned counsel for the private respondents
that the petitioner had been appointed as Assistant Professor in the Higher
Education Department.
It is the case of the applicant/writ petitioner that although he was
appointed as Assistant Professor in the Higher Education Department, he did not
join the said post and he continues to work in the respondent-department.

dated 07.05.2016 passed in the main writ petition, whereby the writ petition was
disposed of on the premise that the writ petitioner had joined the post of
Assistant Professor in the Higher Education Department, deserves to be recalled
and is accordingly recalled. Consequently, the writ petition is restored to its
original number.
The CM is, accordingly, disposed of.
